open_points.subject: OwnerFormField facts and value identity
open_points.text:
The row
gives the field's name, its path in the owner request or its values, with a
tuple's position marked; which of the two it fills; and how its text is
read: as text, as an integer, as true or false, or as an enumeration
member's value.
open_points.question: Are the request path, value path and tuple position facts of OwnerFormField and therefore part of value equality, or are the only identity facts the three items under “Facts”?
options: They are fields and identity facts in addition to name, destination and reading kind
They are fields but do not participate in value identity
They are not fields of OwnerFormField
open_points.default_guess: Treat every datum the row gives as a field and as part of its value identity.

witness.initial: One release needs two rows with the same field name, destination and reading kind but different request paths or tuple positions.
events: The data provider declares both rows in OWNER_FORM_FIELDS.
The owner interface loads the table and compares or indexes OwnerFormField values.
outcomes: The rows are distinct because their paths or positions are facts.
The rows are the same value because the stated Facts are equal, so one row may replace or collapse into the other.
witness.observer: The owner, when one page writes or reads the field at the wrong location.

open_points.subject: OwnerFormField location shape
open_points.text:
its path in the owner request or its values, with a
tuple's position marked
open_points.question: What closed set of location facts does an OwnerFormField contain: a request path, a path into a values collection, a tuple position, or some defined combination, and which of them are optional or mutually exclusive?
options: One discriminated location variant: request path or values path, with tuple position only on the applicable variant
Separate optional request_path, values_path and tuple_position fields
One path field plus an optional tuple_position field
open_points.default_guess: Use a closed discriminated location variant so each row has exactly one unambiguous location.

open_points.subject: OwnerFormField destination
open_points.text: which of the two it fills
open_points.question: What exactly are the two destination values, and is the destination a closed fact of the model identifying “form” versus “query”?
options: A boolean selecting form versus query
open_points.default_guess: Use a closed enum with values for form and query.

open_points.subject: OwnerFormField enumeration parsing
open_points.question: When the reading kind is enumeration, what fact identifies the particular enumeration whose member values are valid?
options: Each row contains an enumeration identity or closed vocabulary reference
All enumeration fields share one global enumeration
The target request path determines the enumeration outside this model
open_points.default_guess: Add a row fact that explicitly identifies the applicable enumeration or vocabulary.

witness.initial: Two owner fields use different enumerations but both are read as an enumeration member's value.
events: The provider publishes both OwnerFormField rows.
The owner submits the same text for each field.
The reader converts each submitted text.
outcomes: The row identifies its enumeration, so the text can be valid for one field and invalid for the other.
The model records only the generic enumeration reading kind, so the reader must infer a domain from external context.
witness.observer: The owner, through whether each submitted field is accepted and which value is produced.

open_points.subject: OwnerFormField provenance
open_points.question: Who creates OwnerFormField values at release construction, and are they copied directly from OWNER_FORM_FIELDS, constructed from some other provider records, or derived by the owner-interface implementation?
options: The data provider authors complete OwnerFormField values directly in OWNER_FORM_FIELDS
The release builder constructs OwnerFormField values from provider source records
The owner interface derives OwnerFormField values at runtime from OWNER_FORM_FIELDS
open_points.default_guess: The data provider authors the complete values directly, and the release exposes them unchanged.

open_points.subject: OwnerFormField product-action use
open_points.text:
A row of the owner form table: one field an owner page writes into a form
or a query, and the owner interface reads back
open_points.question: Which owner-interface product actions create or select these rows and which actions read them, and how does a row identify the page or action to which it applies?
options: Each row contains an owner action or page identity and is used only by that action
One global table applies to every owner-interface action, with request paths alone selecting rows
Separate per-action tables contain OwnerFormField values, so the action is supplied by the containing table
open_points.default_guess: Use separate per-action tables or include an explicit action identity; do not infer action ownership from a field name or path.

witness.initial: The create-project and correct-project pages both contain a field with the same name but use different request locations or permitted destinations.
events: The release provides the owner form table.
The owner opens each page and submits its field.
The owner interface selects rows to build and read each request.
outcomes: Rows are scoped to an action, so each page uses its own row.
Rows are global, so selection must be guessed from name or path and a page may use the other action's row.
witness.observer: The owner, through the request produced or interpreted by each product action.
